title: Implement AppDelegate with transparent overlay NSWindow
description:
## Summary

Create AppDelegate with custom NSWindow configured as a transparent, always-on-top overlay that appears over fullscreen applications.

## Context

macOS requires specific NSWindow configuration to appear above fullscreen apps. Must use `.screenSaver` window level and specific collection behaviors.

## Implementation

1. Create `AppDelegate.swift`:
   ```swift
   import AppKit
   import SwiftUI
   
   class AppDelegate: NSObject, NSApplicationDelegate {
       var overlayWindow: NSWindow!
       
       func applicationDidFinishLaunching(_ notification: Notification) {
           setupOverlayWindow()
       }
       
       private func setupOverlayWindow() {
           // Window configuration here
       }
   }
   ```

2. Configure NSWindow properties:
   ```swift
   window.level = .screenSaver  // Above fullscreen apps
   window.collectionBehavior = [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary]
   window.isOpaque = false
   window.backgroundColor = .clear
   window.ignoresMouseEvents = true  // Click-through
   window.alphaValue = 0.3  // 30% opacity
   window.styleMask = [.borderless]
   window.hasShadow = false
   ```

3. Position window in top-left corner of primary display:
   ```swift
   let screenFrame = NSScreen.main?.frame ?? .zero
   let windowWidth: CGFloat = 300
   let windowHeight: CGFloat = 200
   let origin = CGPoint(x: 20, y: screenFrame.height - windowHeight - 50)
   window.setFrame(NSRect(origin: origin, size: CGSize(width: windowWidth, height: windowHeight)), display: true)
   ```

4. Add NSVisualEffectView for vibrancy blur:
   ```swift
   let visualEffectView = NSVisualEffectView()
   visualEffectView.material = .hudWindow
   visualEffectView.blendingMode = .behindWindow
   visualEffectView.state = .active
   window.contentView = visualEffectView
   ```

5. Wire NSApplicationDelegateAdaptor in `ClaudeCodeMonitorApp.swift`:
   ```swift
   @main
   struct ClaudeCodeMonitorApp: App {
       @NSApplicationDelegateAdaptor(AppDelegate.self) var appDelegate
       
       var body: some Scene {
           Settings { EmptyView() }  // No settings window for now
       }
   }
   ```

## Files to Create/Modify

- Create: `ClaudeCodeMonitor/AppDelegate.swift`
- Modify: `ClaudeCodeMonitor/ClaudeCodeMonitorApp.swift`

title: Implement Session model and SessionStore with unit tests
description:
## Summary

Create the Session data model and SessionStore ObservableObject for managing active Claude Code sessions with full unit test coverage.

## Context

The SessionStore is the central data layer connecting HTTP events to the UI. It must be thread-safe since HTTP events arrive on background threads while UI observes on main thread.

## Implementation

1. Create `Models/Session.swift`:
   ```swift
   import Foundation
   
   struct Session: Identifiable, Equatable {
       let id: String           // session_id from Claude Code
       let workingDirectory: String
       let startedAt: Date
       
       var displayId: String {
           String(id.prefix(8)) + "..."
       }
       
       var displayDirectory: String {
           URL(fileURLWithPath: workingDirectory).lastPathComponent
       }
   }
   ```

2. Create `Services/SessionStore.swift`:
   ```swift
   import Foundation
   import Combine
   
   @MainActor
   final class SessionStore: ObservableObject {
       @Published private(set) var sessions: [Session] = []
       
       func addSession(_ session: Session) {
           guard !sessions.contains(where: { $0.id == session.id }) else { return }
           sessions.append(session)
       }
       
       func removeSession(id: String) {
           sessions.removeAll { $0.id == id }
       }
       
       var sessionCount: Int {
           sessions.count
       }
   }
   ```

3. Create `ClaudeCodeMonitorTests/SessionTests.swift`:
   - Test displayId truncates to 8 chars + "..."
   - Test displayDirectory extracts folder name
   - Test displayDirectory handles edge cases (root, trailing slash)

4. Create `ClaudeCodeMonitorTests/SessionStoreTests.swift`:
   - Test addSession increases count
   - Test removeSession decreases count
   - Test duplicate session ignored
   - Test removeSession with invalid id is no-op
   - Test concurrent add/remove (async test)

## Files to Create

- `ClaudeCodeMonitor/Models/Session.swift`
- `ClaudeCodeMonitor/Services/SessionStore.swift`
- `ClaudeCodeMonitorTests/SessionTests.swift`
- `ClaudeCodeMonitorTests/SessionStoreTests.swift`

## References

- PRD: `/Users/willness/Documents/Projects/N3S/claude-code-monitor/docs/prd.md` (Data Models section)
- Plan: `/Users/willness/.claude/plans/mellow-orbiting-glade.md` (Epic 2)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Session model compiles with correct computed properties
- [ ] SessionStore add/remove works correctly
- [ ] Duplicate sessions are silently ignored
- [ ] All unit tests pass
- [ ] @MainActor ensures thread safety
close_reason: Implemented Session model, SessionStore, and unit tests. All 12 tests passing.

title: Implement HookEvent model and Vapor HTTP server
description:
## Summary

Create the HookEvent Codable model and Vapor-based HTTP server with POST /event and GET /health endpoints.

## Context

Claude Code hooks send HTTP POST requests to localhost:7779 when sessions start/stop. The server must parse JSON payloads and update SessionStore accordingly.

## Implementation

1. Create `Models/HookEvent.swift`:
   ```swift
   import Foundation
   
   struct HookEvent: Codable {
       let sessionId: String
       let eventType: EventType
       let workingDirectory: String?
       let timestamp: Date?
       
       enum EventType: String, Codable {
           case sessionStart = "SessionStart"
           case stop = "Stop"
       }
       
       enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
           case sessionId = "session_id"
           case eventType = "event_type"
           case workingDirectory = "working_directory"
           case timestamp
       }
   }
   ```

2. Create `Services/HTTPServer.swift`:
   ```swift
   import Vapor
   
   final class HTTPServer {
       private var app: Application?
       private let sessionStore: SessionStore
       private let port: Int
       
       init(sessionStore: SessionStore, port: Int = 7779) {
           self.sessionStore = sessionStore
           self.port = port
       }
       
       func start() async throws {
           let app = try await Application.make(.development)
           self.app = app
           
           app.http.server.configuration.hostname = "127.0.0.1"
           app.http.server.configuration.port = port
           
           app.post("event") { [weak self] req async throws -> Response in
               // Parse and handle event
           }
           
           app.get("health") { [weak self] req async -> [String: Any] in
               // Return health status
           }
           
           try await app.startup()
       }
       
       func stop() async {
           try? await app?.asyncShutdown()
       }
   }
   ```

3. Implement POST /event handler:
   - Parse JSON to HookEvent
   - On SessionStart: create Session, add to store
   - On Stop: remove session from store
   - Return {"status": "ok"} on success
   - Return 400 with error for malformed JSON

4. Implement GET /health handler:
   - Return {"status": "healthy", "active_sessions": count}

5. Create `ClaudeCodeMonitorTests/HookEventParsingTests.swift`:
   - Test valid SessionStart payload
   - Test valid Stop payload
   - Test missing required fields
   - Test malformed JSON

6. Create `ClaudeCodeMonitorTests/HTTPServerTests.swift`:
   - Test server starts and responds to health
   - Test POST /event adds session
   - Test POST /event removes session
   - Test malformed JSON returns 400

## Test Script (for manual verification)

```bash
# Start session
curl -X POST http://localhost:7779/event \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"session_id":"test-123","event_type":"SessionStart","working_directory":"/tmp/test"}'

# Check health
curl http://localhost:7779/health

# Stop session
curl -X POST http://localhost:7779/event \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"session_id":"test-123","event_type":"Stop"}'
```

- `ClaudeCodeMonitor/Services/HTTPServer.swift`

- `ClaudeCodeMonitorTests/HTTPServerTests.swift`

title: Create SwiftUI overlay view components
description:
## Summary

Build all SwiftUI view components for the overlay: PulsingDotView, SessionRowView, EmptyStateView, and the main OverlayView.

## Context

The overlay displays a list of active sessions with pulsing status indicators. When no sessions are active, it shows an empty state message. All views must support light/dark mode.

## Implementation

1. Create `Views/PulsingDotView.swift`:
   ```swift
   import SwiftUI
   
   struct PulsingDotView: View {
       @State private var isPulsing = false
       
       var body: some View {
           Circle()
               .fill(Color(red: 52/255, green: 199/255, blue: 89/255))  // #34C759
               .frame(width: 8, height: 8)
               .scaleEffect(isPulsing ? 1.2 : 1.0)
               .opacity(isPulsing ? 0.8 : 1.0)
               .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.8).repeatForever(autoreverses: true), value: isPulsing)
               .onAppear { isPulsing = true }
       }
   }
   ```

2. Create `Views/SessionRowView.swift`:
   ```swift
   import SwiftUI
   
   struct SessionRowView: View {
       let session: Session
       
       var body: some View {
           HStack(spacing: 8) {
               PulsingDotView()
               Text(session.displayId)
                   .font(.system(.body, design: .monospaced))
               Text(session.displayDirectory)
                   .font(.system(.body, design: .monospaced))
                   .foregroundColor(.secondary)
           }
           .padding(.horizontal, 8)
           .padding(.vertical, 4)
       }
   }
   ```

3. Create `Views/EmptyStateView.swift`:
   ```swift
   import SwiftUI
   
   struct EmptyStateView: View {
       var body: some View {
           Text("No active sessions")
               .font(.system(.body, design: .monospaced))
               .foregroundColor(.secondary)
               .padding()
       }
   }
   ```

4. Create `Views/OverlayView.swift`:
   ```swift
   import SwiftUI
   
   struct OverlayView: View {
       @ObservedObject var sessionStore: SessionStore
       
       var body: some View {
           VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0) {
               if sessionStore.sessions.isEmpty {
                   EmptyStateView()
               } else {
                   ForEach(sessionStore.sessions) { session in
                       SessionRowView(session: session)
                   }
               }
           }
           .background(.ultraThinMaterial)
           .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8))
       }
   }
   ```

5. Add SwiftUI previews with mock data for each view

title: Integrate OverlayView with AppDelegate window
description:
## Summary

Connect the SwiftUI OverlayView to the NSWindow in AppDelegate so sessions display in the overlay with live updates.

## Context

The NSWindow uses an NSHostingView to embed SwiftUI content. The OverlayView observes SessionStore and updates automatically when sessions are added/removed via HTTP events.

## Implementation

1. Update `AppDelegate.swift` to embed OverlayView:
   ```swift
   import SwiftUI
   
   class AppDelegate: NSObject, NSApplicationDelegate {
       // ... existing code ...
       
       private func setupOverlayWindow() {
           // ... existing window configuration ...
           
           // Create SwiftUI content
           let overlayView = OverlayView(sessionStore: sessionStore)
           let hostingView = NSHostingView(rootView: overlayView)
           
           // Add to visual effect view
           let visualEffectView = NSVisualEffectView()
           visualEffectView.material = .hudWindow
           visualEffectView.blendingMode = .behindWindow
           visualEffectView.state = .active
           
           hostingView.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
           visualEffectView.addSubview(hostingView)
           
           NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
               hostingView.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: visualEffectView.topAnchor),
               hostingView.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: visualEffectView.leadingAnchor),
               hostingView.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: visualEffectView.trailingAnchor),
               hostingView.bottomAnchor.constraint(equalTo: visualEffectView.bottomAnchor)
           ])
           
           window.contentView = visualEffectView
       }
   }
   ```

2. Ensure window auto-sizes to content (optional enhancement)

## Files to Modify

- `ClaudeCodeMonitor/AppDelegate.swift`

## References

- Plan: `/Users/willness/.claude/plans/mellow-orbiting-glade.md` (Task 4.5)

## Manual End-to-End Test

1. Launch app
2. Overlay should show "No active sessions"
3. Run: `curl -X POST http://localhost:7779/event -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"session_id":"abc12345","event_type":"SessionStart","working_directory":"/Users/test/project"}'`
4. Overlay should show session row with pulsing dot
5. Run: `curl -X POST http://localhost:7779/event -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"session_id":"abc12345","event_type":"Stop"}'`
6. Overlay should return to "No active sessions"

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] OverlayView renders inside NSWindow
- [ ] Empty state visible on launch
- [ ] Sessions appear when added via HTTP
- [ ] Sessions disappear when removed via HTTP
- [ ] UI updates are immediate (sub-100ms)
